implementation: code/signal-trace/pipeline/overlap/fed_replay.py (prepare, capture, record), run by run.sh in this folder
hypothesis: The project's hypothesis: a capability leaves a recurring difference between the traces of correct and wrong answers, and editing the weights where that recurring difference lives repairs the capability. What this run adds to it is material, not a test: on the unchanged original model, one fed word at the heading, the label or the climb's wording makes most of the subtracting fitting answers come out whole (records/development/2026-11-12-path-forward/README.md, 'The label of the line'). Those continuations have so far been read as text only. If the hypothesis is right, the computation after such a fork is where a wrong answer's trace and its own corrected trace part, on one question and one history up to the fork; this run records that computation, every token and all 105 merges, so the request of a correction can be written from the trace and not from the tokens.
why_this_direction: Step 3 asks for the discrepancy along the whole path, and Marcos's direction is that the trace defines the divergence, not the token (past agents used the token as a marker of divergence, and the trace is what should define it; journal/2026-11-10-controlled-training.md: overlap traces are more important than checking answers, since token output is not a reliable measure of success or correctness). The evidence so far that the route is carried by a few words is text evidence: label swap, second feeds, transplant (commits dcae6979 and 0a1a8acf). Each of the three requests the seats are weighing needs the states of these continuations and none exists on disk: Astra's transformation-effect request T_r = x_r + sum_k alpha_rk (y^c_k - x^c_k) needs what each merge adds on a corrected continuation of the same question; Fable's reading of a fork needs the rows before and after it on one history; and the comparison this seat proposed (a route-steering arm against a trace-derived arm) needs the same rows to be judged by the trace. same-prefix-135-original (a7d5b6ea) showed that on the same text, along the recurring direction, the kinds part only at the deciding row; this run gives the rows after it, where the texts differ because one word was fed. It is the next step because it is the one input all three request forms share, it costs one card for well under an hour, and it decides nothing by itself.
repeating_pattern_check: Four things have happened more than once. (1) A divergence or a success was read from tokens and the trace was not looked at; it keeps happening because text is cheap to read and a trace is not on disk when the question comes up. This run puts the trace of every fed continuation on disk, the failed ones included, so the next reading has no reason to fall back on text. (2) Readings were made on the cases that worked (B's repaired answers, the successful subset of a feed) and then did not hold on the rest. This run takes every continuation of the label swap, the heading feed, the heading-and-label feed and the climb feed: the 15 wrong and 14 correct label swaps (8 of the 15 complete; the 14 correct-case controls, of which 6 are not complete after the swap), all 6 heading feeds (1 complete), all 6 heading-and-label feeds (4 complete) and all 7 climb feeds (4 complete), beside all 30 own answers. (3) A capture did not reproduce the pass it was compared with (another card, another recorder build, several tokens read at once). This run replays on the card that generated the texts, feeds one token at a time as generation does, and counts per case the steps whose full scores equal the source pass's to the bit; a case that does not reproduce is reported and its states are not called the states of the generated answer. (4) A run was started to keep moving after a bad number. This one was asked for by the objective's owner as the shared input of the next declared request, during the brainstorm Marcos asked for, and no solve follows from it.

Since then every construction repaired some answers and broke others (B: three breaks; d2-path: the descent added to the climb in 14 of 21 lines it relabelled). The feeds of today were judged by the answer's text and the judge's fields, which Marcos has said is no reliable measure; the heading feed supplied the drop's digit, which makes a heading of the kind the subtracting answers themselves write ('(2 m)'), so its result says nothing against the heading. And this seat's two claims in the brainstorm that were read from text or from a subset were both withdrawn when a trace reading was put beside them (the recurrence over places 168 to 201 is not the label's route; a plain cross-entropy gradient does not confine itself to the changed tokens).
rule: Data roles: these are diagnostic and reference-construction observations of the unchanged original model on the thirty fitting answers. Nothing joins the frozen reference, the cohort, the fitting folds or any score; an answer after a fed token is no model's own result; no weight is solved and no target, mask or threshold is made here. The answers no fit uses are not read, and reserved-40b is not opened (the question lookup passes its folder over by name). No answer is generated: every token of every text but its last is supplied; the last token the model writes itself, because the recorder refuses a supplied end-of-generation token and refuses supplied text that leaves the model no token of its own (one unforced last step in each of the 78 cases; see revisions). The run itself checks, step by step, that the model's own first choice is the text's token everywhere except at the forced steps, so the text is shown here to be what the original writes under those feeds. The original model file is read only. Deviations, stated: (a) the method's design condition names GPU0 for everything compared; these passes run on card 1 (RTX 5070 Ti), because the texts were generated there and GPU0 is held by another project's process, so nothing here is compared with a GPU0 recording and a later comparison across cards needs its own reproduction reading; (b) the recorder's raw stream of one question at a time is written to a temporary folder outside this run folder (the session's scratch, same disk) and removed once kept/ holds it losslessly, every state checked bit for bit against the raw stream first and the raw files' sha256 kept; everything the run keeps is in its own folder; (c) the cases' token ids and forced steps come from this seat's committed development records (cases_built_from), which are not round-two inputs; they are frozen in cases/ with their sha256, and they are texts of the same original model on the same card.

cases.derivation: Every answer of the label swap's thirty fitting answers gives its own answer on card 1 (30). Every continuation those records hold is taken, none chosen by its outcome: the label swap's 29 (one correct answer has no such line), the heading feed's 6, the heading-and-label feed's 6, the climb feed's 7: 78 cases, 39,340 answer tokens, 52,754 positions with the prompts (cases/index.json). The transplant's 27 passes and the sign feed's 14 are not in this capture: the request named the label, heading and climb continuations, and the two would add roughly 15 GiB kept (a transplant shares no prefix with the own answer); stated as a gap, not a judgment of them.
cases.scales_with: The feeds on record and the fitting answers.

forced_steps.derivation: A forced step of a case is a step at which its source pass supplied a token that was not the model's own first choice there (the source pass's own record of each step: selection 'teacher' and greedy_token != selected). For the label, heading and heading-and-label cases this must equal the steps the development record names, or prepare stops; for the climb cases it is the label's step and the one or two tokens of the climb's word that the model would not have written. The first forced step is the least of them.

one_question_per_recorder_call.derivation: A recorder call reads one question: its own answer and its continuations (1 to 5 cases; the largest raw stream of one question is 5.1 GiB = its positions x 247 tensors x 6144 bytes). No count is chosen: the unit is the question, because a continuation is compared with the own answer of its question and both are then read in one call of one process, and because the card's lock is released between questions so another seat's job is not held behind the whole capture.
one_question_per_recorder_call.scales_with: The number of continuations a question has.

what_is_kept_per_position.derivation: That capture (same recorder, same retention) holds 466,360,320 bytes for 308 positions and 137 output-norm rows: 75,905 tensors of 1536 float32 = 246 x 308 + 137, so a position has 246 tensors (the scaled embedding and seven per layer) and a step one more: 247 at most, 1.52 MB. Of the seven per layer, three are what a merge adds; the other four are sums and one product the engine makes from them, which the capture checks bit for bit at every position before it keeps only the embedding and the 105 added parts: 106 tensors a position and the output norm at each step, 107 at most. For a continuation the positions through the row that writes its first forced token are kept once, in the own answer, where they are bit for bit equal: 38,717 of the 52,754 positions are then kept, 23.7 GiB (32.2 GiB if no shared prefix were equal).
what_is_kept_per_position.scales_with: The recorder's retention scope, the model's depth and width, and where each case's first forced step lies.

layer_output_scale.derivation: blk.L.layer_output_scale.weight, one float32 per layer read from the original model file at the listed offset. The layer's exit is its last sum times this value in float32; the capture checks that against the recorded exit at every position and layer and stops at the first difference.

disk_margin.derivation: The machine's disk rule as that run applies it: nothing starts unless what it writes and 40 GB beside it fit on root (read as GiB here, as that script's df -BG does). Here per question: its raw stream and what is kept of it, read from free space before each recorder call.

card.derivation: Card 1, where the own answers were captured and every feed pass ran, so that a step's full scores can be compared with the source pass's to the bit. The runner takes /run/user/1000/gpu1.lock itself for each question and waits for 11,000 MiB free.
card.scales_with: The card and the recorder's build; a comparison across either needs its own reproduction reading.

prediction: Three statements about the replay, each of which the record command counts. (1) Reproduction: in every one of the 48 continuations, every step has the source pass's full scores to the bit (the sha256 of all 262,144 scores), as same-prefix-135-original found for its five regenerated prefixes; the own answers come from the solver's own-answer pass, whose per-step scores this run does not read; they are checked through (3). (2) Unchanged before the choice: in all 48 continuations the positions through the row that writes the first forced token hold the own answer's first incoming states and all 105 added parts bit for bit, because a later token cannot reach an earlier position and the passes read one token at a time. (3) The text is the model's own under the feeds: in all 78 cases the model's own first choice differs from the text's token only at forced steps (never, in the 30 own answers), and in all 78 cases the one token the model writes is the text's last token (the end-of-generation token in the 74 texts that ended by themselves). The paired same-history row is described, not predicted: nothing on record says at which merges a swapped word changes the next position most.
would_weaken_it: (1) A continuation with steps whose scores differ from its source pass: then capture mode, or supplying every token, is not the arithmetic of the pass that generated the text, and that case's states are not called the generated answer's states. (2) A continuation whose positions before the first forced choice differ from the own answer's: then two readings of one history differ on this card and no paired comparison on this capture is exact; the case keeps all its positions and says so. (3) An own first choice that differs from the text at a step that was not forced: then that text is not what the original writes under the declared feeds. None of these can weaken the project's hypothesis, and none can support it: this run records, it does not compare groups. What a reading of these states could later weaken is the route account of today's feeds: if, after the fork, a corrected continuation's rows are no nearer the correct answers' computation than the own wrong answer's rows are, the fed word changed the text and not the computation the hypothesis is about.
